Connect a local MCP client or use qz from the terminal:

```bash
npm run qz -- connect
npm run qz -- status
npm run qz -- browsers
npm run qz -- mcp
npm run qz -- create "Summarize the current page." --wait
npm run qz -- create "Compare these two laptops." --title "Research" --stream
npm run qz -- send TASK_ID "Add the source links." --stream
npm run qz -- send TASK_ID "Focus on open-source options." --steer --stream
npm run qz -- tasks
npm run qz -- show TASK_ID
npm run qz -- submit TASK_ID '{"selectedIds":["option-a"]}' --stream
npm run qz -- approve TASK_ID --wait
npm run qz -- reject TASK_ID
npm run qz -- watch TASK_ID --stream
npm run qz -- cancel TASK_ID
npm run qz -- data
npm run qz -- data export TABLE --format xlsx
npm run qz -- images export COLLECTION
npm run qz -- skills --query research
npm run qz -- skills export NAME
npm run qz -- settings get model
npm run qz -- settings set vision true
npm run qz -- automations
npm run qz -- stop
```

`connect` starts the local service and opens its connection page for first pairing. The first
browser is named `default`; repeating the command reuses an online connection. `status` shows the
actual service address and `mcp` prints its MCP URL. The default port is 18765, with a free-port
fallback when occupied; `connect --port PORT` requests another port. A running service keeps its
existing address. Use the reported address when connecting another profile.

To pair a chosen browser Profile from the shell:

```bash
npm run qz -- connect --no-open --name work --json
```

Open `result.url` in that Profile and verify its online UUID with `browsers --json`.
`--no-open` returns the URL immediately. `--name` sets or updates the identifier of the Profile
opening it; omit it to preserve an existing name or allocate `default`, `browser-2`, and so on.
`connect --name work` opens the URL and also returns without waiting for pairing. Neither mode
accepts `--client`. See [platform launch commands](cli.md#pair-a-selected-browser-from-the-shell).
Pairing is also available in **qz Settings → Advanced → CLI**.

`--client NAME|UUID` selects a browser for task and resource commands. With one online browser,
selection is automatic; with several, it is required. Unknown or offline selections fail without
falling back. Names are persistent and case-sensitive. Disconnect one profile in its qz Settings;
`stop` stops the service and disconnects all browsers. To release an offline name, run
`npm run qz -- browsers forget NAME`. Each command and its suggested next steps remain bound to
the resolved profile UUID.

Connections require opening a pairing URL or the settings action. Ordinary connection failures
pause after three attempts; reopen the URL in that Profile or use its settings to retry. Use the current CLI and extension together. Source edits do not
restart a working service. To update, finish current tasks, run `stop`, update and reload the extension, then run `connect`. See
[connection and upgrade details](cli.md#connect-and-stop).

`create` accepts the task text directly, with an optional title.
`--wait` waits for the result; `--stream` also displays progress. Both stay connected through
questions and permission requests, then continue automatically after you respond. Pending output
includes the full request, field IDs, option values, and a submission template. Use `show TASK_ID` to
read the request again, answer fields with `submit`, continue a confirmation with
`approve`, or decline it with `reject`. Responses bind to the current wait; `--wait-id ID` selects a
specific request. `submit`, `approve`, and `reject` also accept `--wait` and `--stream`. Review the displayed
application consent notice before approving. Native Chrome permissions require a click in the
side panel; the CLI preserves the wait and tells you where to confirm. Respond in the side panel or
another terminal while the original command keeps watching. `watch` follows an existing task.
Task observation has no default time limit. Add `--timeout SECONDS` to set a total deadline,
including user-input pauses. Each individual connection request remains bounded (180 seconds by
default). Timeout or Ctrl-C ends watching; `watch TASK_ID --stream` resumes observation and
`cancel TASK_ID` stops the task.

If the selected browser has no matching task, `show` fails with `task_not_found` and exit code 1.
`watch` reports `task_deleted` and suggests listing tasks for the same browser UUID. Check the ID
and browser selection with `tasks --client CLIENT_UUID` and `browsers` before watching again.

`send TASK_ID MESSAGE` follows up on a specific task and supports the same waiting options. A busy
task queues the follow-up for its next run. Add `--steer` to deliver the message to the current run
at its next safe boundary. Both start a new run when idle; pending questions and permissions still
require a response. Streaming shows responses after the submitted message.

`data` and `images` list, export, or delete saved tables and image collections. Table exports support
`xlsx` (default) and `csv`; image collections and individual user-installed Skills export as ZIPs
through Chrome downloads. `skills` lists or searches installed Skills; `skills show NAME` reads one,
`skills read NAME PATH` reads a resource in chunks, and `skills tools -s TASK_ID` lists contributions.
`settings` reads redacted configuration and editable fields; `settings set KEY VALUE` updates a
field, and `settings set -` reads a JSON patch from stdin. Use stdin for credentials.
`automations` lists saved automations, and `automations run ID` starts one. Export results include
the download status and path when available; check pending downloads in `chrome://downloads`.

Exports accept `--filename NAME`; `skills --scope site` filters Skills by scope. CLI commands reuse
one MCP connection for all their requests. Use `--client NAME|UUID` to select a profile from `browsers`.
MCP supports the same task waiting, streaming, and input flows, plus direct browser tool calls and
diagnostic logs; see the [operation mapping](cli.md#task-and-resource-operations).

Interactive terminals show text; pipes receive JSON. `--json` and `--plain` select the output
format explicitly. `--no-color` or `NO_COLOR` disables color. JSON waiting and streaming produce one
final result on stdout, with pending-input notices on stderr. The installed CLI requires Node.js 22 or later.
See the [CLI and MCP reference](cli.md) for short options, stdin input, and
MCP browser tools.

```bash
node scripts/source-inventory.mjs --baseline <git-ref> --check-reduction
node scripts/vendor/assets.mjs --check
```

The first command compares source size against a commit; the second checks that installed runtime
dependencies match the lockfile. For setup outside the extension, see the [local MCP

# Design system

Build capability layouts with the shared tokens, `qz-*` controls, and `qz:` utilities. The Side
Panel and exported Session HTML use the same compiled skin. Begin with the [capability
guide](../src/capabilities/README.md) to register a page or renderer; this guide covers its public
styling contract.

## CSS ownership and cascade

[The default theme](../src/themes/default/index.css) declares the cascade: `theme → base → vendor →
components → utilities`. It imports [tokens](../src/themes/default/tokens.css), [base
styles](../src/themes/default/base.css), [controls](../src/themes/default/controls.css), and
[utilities](../src/themes/default/utilities.css). [sidepanel.css](../src/sidepanel/sidepanel.css)
combines the selected theme with feature styles. Feature and capability CSS stays with its owning
module; the build includes it in the complete skin.

Tokens own semantic colors, fonts, density, radii, and motion. Tailwind 4 maps them with `@theme
inline`; the build imports Tailwind utilities with the project theme. Base styles use a 13px root
font and 4px spacing units. Capability styles join the build through their own `ui.css`.

Use template utilities for ordinary layout and spacing. Shared controls, generated Markdown, complex
states, and animation belong in scoped `components` rules. Utilities can override component
defaults; keep an overridable property's hover, responsive, and disabled behavior consistent with
that cascade. Third-party styles enter through a thin `vendor` layer wrapper; retain upstream files
and licenses.

## Controls and tokens

Use native button/input semantics and the shared control states.

| Purpose | Public classes |
| --- | --- |
| Buttons | `qz-btn` with `qz-btn--primary`, `qz-btn--secondary`, `qz-btn--ghost`, or `qz-btn--danger`; sizes `qz-btn--xs/sm/lg` |
| Icon buttons | `qz-icon-btn` with `qz-icon-btn--secondary` or `qz-icon-btn--danger`; sizes `qz-icon-btn--xs/sm/md` |
| Fields | `qz-field`, `qz-field-label`, `qz-field-hint`; combine `qz-field qz-select` for selects |
| Choice inputs | `qz-checkbox`, `qz-radio`, `qz-switch`, driven by native input state |
| Result choices | `qz-choice-card` family, built with `renderResultChoice` from SDK DOM; single-column cards with a native radio or checkbox |
| Popovers and menus | `qz-popover`, `qz-menu`, `qz-menu-item` |
| Lists and decisions | `qz-list-toolbar` and `qz-decision-dialog` families; use the SDK dialog interaction |
| Scrolling | `qz-scroll`; add `qz-scroll--native` for native scrollbars |

Control overrides use the declared `--qz-control-*`, `--qz-field-*`, and `--qz-popover-*` variables.
`--qz-choice-card-text-scale` scales result-card text and line height together; it defaults to `1`.
Preserve accessible names, keyboard focus, and disabled semantics. DOM helpers and renderer
contracts are available through [SDK DOM](../src/sdk/sidepanel/dom.ts) and
[renderers](../src/sdk/sidepanel/renderers.ts).

Use `renderResultChoice(document, options)` for selectable tool results. Supply a unique `id`, the
form field `name`, a stable result `value`, and its `label`; `multiple` selects checkbox or radio
semantics. Optional `description`, short `meta` labels, an HTTP(S) `imageUrl`, and an HTTP(S) `url`
add detail. The source link sits outside the selection label so opening a source preserves the
selection. Pass `checked` and `disabled` from the owning form. The helper owns no listeners or
state; its native input events bubble to the form, which handles validation and submission.

Result cards use the theme's field, choice, and focus tokens. Keep them in one column in narrow
panels, with metadata wrapping below the title and a small optional thumbnail. Group related cards
with an accessible field label; use the existing form controls for the selection count and action.
Title, description, metadata, and source text share the 18px `--choice-card-line-height`. Separate
text blocks by 2px, cards by 8px, and use the small field padding token (8px) for card insets.

| --- | --- |
| `qz:bg-surface`, `qz:bg-surface-muted`, `qz:bg-surface-elevated` | `--bg-primary`, `--bg-tertiary`, `--bg-elevated` |
| `qz:text-foreground`, `qz:text-secondary`, `qz:text-muted` | `--text-primary`, `--text-secondary`, `--text-muted` |
| `qz:text-danger`, `qz:text-success`, `qz:text-warning` | `--red`, `--green`, `--orange` |
| `qz:border-border`, `qz:border-focus` | `--border`, `--border-focus` |
| `qz:font-ui`, `qz:font-code`, `qz:text-body` | `--font-sans`, `--font-mono`, `--field-font-md` |
| `qz:rounded-control`, `qz:rounded-panel`, `qz:shadow-popover` | `--control-radius`, `--radius-lg`, `--shadow-lg` |

## Template example

The `qz:` utility prefix precedes variants, as in `qz:hover:bg-surface-muted`. It is distinct from
the `qz-*` component classes. Keep semantic classes and IDs used by interaction, tests, and skins.

```html
<section class="example-panel qz:flex qz:flex-col qz:gap-2 qz:p-4 qz:bg-surface qz:rounded-panel">
  <label class="qz-field-label" for="example-name">Name</label>
  <input id="example-name" class="qz-field" dir="auto">
  <button type="button" class="qz-btn qz-btn--primary">Save</button>
</section>
```

Use localized labels in production templates. The build discovers complete class strings in HTML and
TypeScript. Enumerate dynamic states explicitly:

```ts
const tones = { ready: "qz:text-success", failed: "qz:text-danger" };
element.classList.remove(...Object.values(tones));
element.classList.add(tones[state]);
```

Use complete class names as above. For dynamic numeric values, use CSS variables in scoped rules.
Cloned templates and later `className` assignments must retain the same layout classes as the
initial template.

## Select a theme

Themes live under [src/themes/](../src/themes/README.md). To select another theme at build time,
create a sibling directory with an `index.css` and change the first import in
[sidepanel.css](../src/sidepanel/sidepanel.css):

```css
@import "../themes/custom/index.css";
```

For a variation of the default theme, the new entry can import `../default/index.css` and override
semantic tokens in `@layer theme`. An independent theme implements the same public contract. Set
`data-qingzhou-skin` on the stylesheet link in [sidepanel.html](../src/sidepanel/sidepanel.html) to
the theme's name when recording that name in HTML exports.

Keep the remaining feature imports. Each theme preserves the public semantic tokens, `qz-*`
controls, `qz:` utilities, layer order, and DOM contract described here. Rebuild using the
[development commands](commands.md); the output remains `sidepanel/sidepanel.css` and includes the
selected theme, feature styles, and enabled capability styles.

## Color schemes, direction, and export

Semantic tokens respond to `prefers-color-scheme`; the same utility class works in light and dark
mode. Use logical margins, padding, alignment, and popover anchors so the root `dir` can control
layout. Code, shortcuts, URLs, and technical inputs remain LTR; free text inputs can use
`dir="auto"`. Preserve image orientation and stored data. See [localization](localization.md) for
language behavior.

[Skin runtime](../src/sidepanel/ui/skin-runtime.ts) reads the active skin link and supplies its
complete compiled CSS to exports. Static renderers produce readable standalone content. Selectors
cover both live containers and static output, including containers styled with `display: contents`.
The panel stores its reading-size preference locally; exports use the skin's text size.

Verify relevant fixtures in both color schemes, narrow panels, RTL, keyboard/focus/disabled states,
reduced motion, and exported HTML. Use the [test guide](../tests/README.md) to select browser and
visual checks; contribution requirements, including pixel comparisons for visual migrations, live in
[AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md).

# Translate qz

Keep source messages with the feature that owns them, and language packs in a capability.
Translations run locally through contributed language descriptors. The public contracts are in the
[catalog SDK](../src/sdk/shared/i18n-definition.ts) and [translation
SDK](../src/sdk/shared/i18n.ts).

## Add or change interface copy

Define a stable namespace and key with English and Simplified Chinese source text. Translate whole
sentences and preserve named parameters. For example, a feature's `messages.ts` can contain:

```ts
import { defineMessages } from "#sdk/shared/i18n-definition";

export default defineMessages("example", {
  saved: { en: "Saved {name}", "zh-CN": "已保存 {name}" },
});
```

Export that catalog as `translations` from the capability's `index.ts`. Create its translator where
the feature needs text:

```ts
import { createTranslator } from "#sdk/shared/i18n";
import messages from "./messages.js";

const t = createTranslator(messages);
label.textContent = t("saved", { name: displayName });
```

Translations are plain text. Use `textContent` or the existing HTML/attribute escaper for markup.
Preserve user data, model output, page content, imported Skill documents, model IDs, commands, enum
values, storage keys, and stored diagnostics verbatim.

Add other translations under [language catalogs](../src/capabilities/i18n/locales/), in
`<language>/<namespace>.json`. For the example above, `ja/example.json` would contain:

```json
{ "example.saved": "{name}を保存しました" }
```

Write short, idiomatic actions and sentence-case labels. English uses **chat** for a conversation,
**task** for work the agent executes, and **session** for technical runtime or authentication
contexts. Errors should explain what happened and what the user can do next. Review loading, empty,
error and success states in their actual controls; a grammatically correct label may still be
unclear or clipped.

## Add a language

Add its native name, Chrome locale, optional matching aliases, reading direction and catalog path to
[locales.ts](../src/capabilities/i18n/locales.ts). A separate capability may contribute its own
`locales` instead. Keep catalog paths inside that package. The build rejects duplicate declarations,
unknown message keys and mismatched parameters, then compiles native Chrome `_locales` resources.
Only the selected catalog is loaded at startup; missing translations retain authored fallbacks.

Use the existing regional aliases, especially for Chinese scripts. Unsupported languages fall back
to English. The language selector is generated from installed descriptors and offers **Follow
browser** alongside each native language name.

Model-facing instructions and detailed tool schemas retain maintained English and Simplified Chinese
versions; other languages fall back to English. Keep identifiers and execution behavior stable.
External Skill and MCP descriptions remain unchanged, and the model still follows the user's
requested response language.

Built-in approval cards resolve their titles and disclosures from the stored approval type in the
panel's current language. Apply this to pending and resolved history entries. Keep model-authored
questions and form labels verbatim; translation belongs to the display projection and preserves
the stored transcript.

## Preserve language and history behavior

Resolve long-lived display metadata through getters, as in the [provider
presets](../src/capabilities/models/presets.ts). The Background captures localized descriptions for
each new run; existing runs retain their language snapshot. Keep `withLanguage` within synchronous
calls; it restores the previous scope on return.

Declare canonical tool titles in `defineMessages`' `historicalLabels` option. The compiled alias
index recognizes translated titles from saved conversations and displays known titles in the current
language. Custom titles and stored snapshots remain unchanged. Use separate `Short` message keys for
compact cards and timeline labels while preserving the canonical history mapping.

Read and save preferences through the SDK. The [language settings
form](../src/capabilities/i18n/ui.ts) reloads the panel only after every participating form in the
shared settings tab has saved its current revision. Failed or cancelled saves must leave the draft
recoverable. Background tasks keep running; the reopened panel initializes with the saved language.
Chrome's extension-management labels independently follow Chrome's language, using base [manifest
messages](../src/_locales/) and contributed manifest translations.

Use `轻舟`, `輕舟` and `軽舟` for Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese and Japanese; other languages
use lowercase `qz`. Keep code symbols and user content unchanged. Ordinary empty chats show the
localized `core.tagline`; initial task suggestions hide it. Keep the tagline natural in each
language and preserve the suggestion's editable-draft behavior.

## Check text, layout and exports

Run the relevant catalog checks and inspect the rendered interface:

```bash
npm run build
npm test -- unit --match i18n
npm test -- unit --match language
npm test -- unit --match locales
npm test -- playwright i18n-language-settings.spec.mjs language-packs-i18n.spec.mjs tool-history-i18n.spec.mjs
```

Check both color schemes at a 320px panel width, including selected options, long labels, focus and
keyboard operation. Arabic uses RTL layout while code, URLs and technical tokens keep LTR order.
Preserve image orientation. Follow the shared [design system](design-system.md) for controls that
must accommodate longer copy. Open an exported chat offline and check its language, direction and
